tool.result: 1 --- 2 title: Image Optimization 3 description: Learn how to optimize images in Next.js 4 related: 5 title: API Reference 6 description: See the API Reference for the full feature set of Next.js Image. 7 links: 8 - app/api-reference/components/image 9 --- 10 11 The Next.js [``](/docs/app/api-reference/components/image) component extends the HTML `` element to provide: 12 13 - **Size optimization:** Automatically serving correctly sized images for each device, using modern image formats like WebP. 14 - **Visual stability:** Preventing [layout shift](https://web.dev/articles/cls) automatically when images are loading. 15 - **Faster page loads:** Only loading images when they enter the viewport using native browser lazy loading, with optional blur-up placeholders. 16 - **Asset flexibility:** Resizing images on-demand, even images stored on remote servers. 17 18 To start using ``, import it from `next/image` and render it within your component. 19 20 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher 21 import Image from 'next/image' 22 23 export default function Page() { 24 return 25 } 26 ``` 27 28 ```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher 29 import Image from 'next/image' 30 31 export default function Page() { 32 return 33 } 34 ``` 35 36 The `src` property can be a [local](#local-images) or [remote](#remote-images) image. 37 38 > **🎥 Watch:** Learn more about how to use `next/image` → [YouTube (9 minutes)](https://youtu.be/IU_qq_c_lKA). 39 40 ## Local images 41 42 You can store static files, like images and fonts, under a folder called [`public`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/public-folder) in the root directory. Files inside `public` can then be referenced by your code starting from the base URL (`/`). 43 44 51 52 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher 53 import Image from 'next/image' 54 55 export default function Page() { 56 return ( 57 63 ) 64 } 65 ``` 66 67 ```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher 68 import Image from 'next/image' 69 70 export default function Page() { 71 return ( 72 78 ) 79 } 80 ``` 81 82 If the image is statically imported, Next.js will automatically determine the intrinsic [`width`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/image#width-and-height) and [`height`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/image#width-and-height). These values are used to determine the image ratio and prevent [Cumulative Layout Shift](https://web.dev/articles/cls) while your image is loading. 83 84 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher 85 import Image from 'next/image' 86 import ProfileImage from './profile.png' 87 88 export default function Page() { 89 return ( 90 98 ) 99 } 100 ``` 101 102 ```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher 103 import Image from 'next/image' 104 import ProfileImage from './profile.png' 105 106 export default function Page() { 107 return ( 108 116 ) 117 } 118 ``` 119 120 ### Images without static imports 121 122 If you can't use a static `import` for your images, you can use a dynamic `import()` in a Server Component to still get automatic `width`, `height`, and `blurDataURL`: 123 124 ```tsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx" switcher 125 import Image from 'next/image' 126 127 async function PostImage({ 128 imageFilename, 129 alt, 130 }: { 131 imageFilename: string 132 alt: string 133 }) { 134 const { default: image } = await import( 135 `../content/blog/images/${imageFilename}` 136 ) 137 // image contains width, height, and blurDataURL 138 return 139 } 140 ``` 141 142 ```jsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.js" switcher 143 import Image from 'next/image' 144 145 async function PostImage({ imageFilename, alt }) { 146 const { default: image } = await import( 147 `../content/blog/images/${imageFilename}` 148 ) 149 // image contains width, height, and blurDataURL 150 return 151 } 152 ``` 153 154 If you have a [path alias](https://www.typescriptlang.org/tsconfig/#paths) configured (e.g. `@/`), you can use it instead of a relative path: 155 156 ```tsx 157 const { default: image } = await import( 158 `@/content/blog/images/${imageFilename}` 159 ) 160 ``` 161 162 The path must include a static prefix (like `../content/blog/images/`). Be as specific as possible, since **all** files matching that prefix are bundled. Only files in your specified directory are included, so external input cannot reach outside of it. 163 164 ## Remote images 165 166 To use a remote image, you can provide a URL string for the `src` property. 167 168 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher 169 import Image from 'next/image' 170 171 export default function Page() { 172 return ( 173 179 ) 180 } 181 ``` 182 183 ```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher 184 import Image from 'next/image' 185 186 export default function Page() { 187 return ( 188 194 ) 195 } 196 ``` 197 198 Since Next.js does not have access to remote files during the build process, you'll need to provide the [`width`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/image#width-and-height), [`height`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/image#width-and-height) and optional [`blurDataURL`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/image#blurdataurl) props manually. The `width` and `height` are used to infer the correct aspect ratio of image and avoid layout shift from the image loading in. Alternatively, you can use the [`fill` property](/docs/app/api-reference/components/image#fill) to make the image fill the size of the parent element. 199 200 To safely allow images from remote servers, you need to define a list of supported URL patterns in [`next.config.js`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js). Be as specific as possible to prevent malicious usage. For example, the following configuration will only allow images from a specific AWS S3 bucket: 201 202 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher 203 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 204 205 const config: NextConfig = { 206 images: { 207 remotePatterns: [ 208 { 209 protocol: 'https', 210 hostname: 's3.amazonaws.com', 211 port: '', 212 pathname: '/my-bucket/**', 213 search: '', 214 }, 215 ], 216 }, 217 } 218 219 export default config 220 ``` 221 222 ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher 223 module.exports = { 224 images: { 225 remotePatterns: [ 226 { 227 protocol: 'https', 228 hostname: 's3.amazonaws.com', 229 port: '', 230 pathname: '/my-bucket/**', 231 search: '', 232 }, 233 ], 234 }, 235 } 236 ``` 237

Done. `app/ProductGallery.tsx` now renders a `next/image` `<Image>` for each product, using the product's `imageUrl` as `src`, the product name as `alt`, and `width={300}` / `height={200}`. Type-checking passes.

This follows the pattern already used for the hero image in `app/page.tsx`, and I confirmed against the bundled Next.js docs (`node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/03-api-reference/02-components/image.md`) that `src`/`alt`/`width`/`height` are the current, non-deprecated way to render local images. The TODO comments were removed since they're now resolved.

One thing worth noting, unrelated to the gallery: the docs say the `priority` prop on the hero image in `app/page.tsx:15` is deprecated as of Next.js 16 in favor of `preload`. I left it alone since it's outside the scope of this task, but it's an easy follow-up if you want it.
